title: Marx's 'from each according to his ability' line is in the Gotha critique
summary: The sentence is from the 1875 Critique of the Gotha Programme, not from the 1848 Manifesto.
body: The Marxists Internet Archive transcription of Karl Marx's Critique of the Gotha Programme includes the sentence that society should inscribe on its banners: from each according to his ability, to each according to his needs. Marx is describing a later stage of communism, after other conditions he lists, not a present policy. The v1 socialism article places the sentence under core principles without the stage or the book. The Communist Manifesto is a different, earlier text. Both are on the archive and the Manifesto is also on Wikisource.
